long_biography.plain_text:
At twelve, Ray Dalio used money earned as a golf caddie to buy shares in Northeast Airlines. The company was acquired and his investment tripled, an early success he later credited more to luck than insight. Finance studies and an MBA led to commodities work and the creation of Bridgewater.

Dalio built the firm around research into recurring economic cause-and-effect relationships, turning investment rules into systematic tools. Daily Observations circulated his thinking to institutional clients, and a World Bank mandate became Bridgewater's first institutional account. He also shaped an internal culture around explicit principles, candid disagreement and testing ideas, methods he later set out in books and educational projects.
